title: Binary Search & Parametric Search
relevance: High (appears constantly as optimal/hidden constraints in arrays)
company_notes: Resource allocation OAs (e.g. Amazon: partition packages into K days minimizing maximum daily weight); speed/rate problems (minimum rate to finish in H hours, Koko Eating Bananas); subsequence/subarray optimization (pick length-K subsequence minimizing maximum difference → sorting + BS); hidden parametric float BS (maximum non-overlapping circle radius).

phases.goal: Establish that the candidate spots binary search / binary search on answer from wording and constraints.

must_hit.point: Wording like "minimize the maximum" or "maximize the minimum" is a hard giveaway for binary search on answer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those phrases and says the answer is the boundary of a monotone feasibility predicate.

must_hit.point: "Find the smallest K such that..." signals binary search on answer rather than a direct closed formula.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says search over candidate K values with a yes/no check, not iterate all answers linearly.

must_hit.point: When the answer range is massive (e.g. up to 10^{14}) but a guessed answer validates in O(N), reach for binary search on answer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites huge answer bounds plus cheap validation as the classic parametric-search tell.

probes: What phrases or constraint shapes make you reach for binary search on answer instead of a linear scan?
If the answer can be huge but checking a candidate is cheap, what technique do you use?

hints.1: Look at the ask: min/max of a constrained quantity, or smallest K with a property.
hints.2: Tie "minimize the maximum" / "maximize the minimum" / "smallest K such that" to a monotone check.
hints.3: Say: those phrases or a 10^{14}-scale answer with O(N) validation → binary search on the answer.

phases.goal: Get the candidate to state monotonicity and the isValid(mid) formulation before coding.

must_hit.point: If the search space is monotonic, binary search finds the boundary (minimum or maximum valid answer).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that once feasibility flips from false to true (or vice versa), binary search isolates the boundary.

must_hit.point: Binary search on answer centers on formulating an isValid(mid) predicate for a guessed mid.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes guessing mid then checking whether mid is a feasible answer under the problem constraints.

must_hit.point: Monotonicity examples: if a task can finish in X time it can finish in X+1; if a number is ≥ k, all larger numbers are ≥ k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives one of those two monotone implications to justify searching the boundary.

probes: What must be true of the search space before binary search on answer is valid?
How do you set up the check you run on mid for a parametric problem?

hints.1: Think about whether better answers stay feasible as the parameter moves one way.
hints.2: Name a monotone predicate and an isValid(mid) that returns yes/no for a guessed answer.
hints.3: Say: monotone space → search the min/max valid boundary; implement that as isValid(mid) (e.g. finish in X ⇒ finish in X+1).

phases.goal: Confirm they can write bound logic, the integer loop template, and safe floating-point iteration.

must_hit.point: Can write std::lower_bound / std::upper_bound logic (or Python bisect) from scratch without off-by-one errors.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches a lo/hi loop that lands on first ≥ / first > without fencing off-by-one.

must_hit.point: Integer binary search template: l = min_possible, r = max_possible; while(l <= r) { mid = l + (r-l)/2; ... }.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites that loop shape and mid = l + (r-l)/2 rather than (l+r)/2 overflow risk.

must_hit.point: Floating-point binary search uses for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) instead of while(r - l > EPS) to avoid precision TLE.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prefers a fixed ~100 iterations over an EPS-based while loop.

probes: Write the integer binary-search loop skeleton you actually use in contests.
How do you binary-search a floating-point answer without precision TLE?

hints.1: Start from lower/upper bound logic and a lo/hi while loop.
hints.2: Use l/r = min/max possible, mid = l+(r-l)/2; for floats prefer a fixed iteration count.
hints.3: Spell: while(l <= r) with mid = l+(r-l)/2; floats: for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) not while(r-l > EPS).

phases.goal: Confirm they know the log search-space cost and that each mid check is linear in N when that is the validation cost.

must_hit.point: On a monotonic search space, the boundary is found in O(log(search space)) binary-search steps.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States logarithmic steps over the answer/index range, not linear enumeration of candidates.

must_hit.point: When validating a guessed answer takes O(N), that is the per-mid check cost paired with the log search.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates cheap O(N) feasibility from the log number of guesses over a huge answer range.

probes: What is the search complexity once the space is monotonic?
If checking a candidate answer scans the array once, what cost do you quote per mid?

hints.1: Separate number of guesses from cost of one guess.
hints.2: Guesses are logarithmic in the search space; a full-array check is O(N).
hints.3: Say: O(log(search space)) steps, each validating in O(N) when that is the predicate cost.

phases.goal: Catch off-by-one bounds bugs, EPS float loops, and missing min-max wording cues.

must_hit.point: Off-by-one errors in hand-rolled lower_bound / upper_bound break first/last position and bound queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Warns about inclusive/exclusive hi updates and landing on the wrong first ≥ / first > index.

must_hit.point: Floating-point while(r - l > EPS) risks precision TLE; prefer a fixed for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) loop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects EPS while-loops under tight TL in favor of ~100 iterations.

must_hit.point: Failing to treat "minimize the maximum" / "maximize the minimum" as a BS-on-answer signal leads to slower or wrong approaches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Immediately maps that wording to parametric binary search (e.g. Book Allocation / Painter's Partition style).

probes: What goes wrong if your lower/upper bound loop is off by one?
Why avoid while(r - l > EPS) for contest floating-point binary search?

hints.1: Think bounds landing and float termination conditions.
hints.2: Hand-rolled bisect off-by-ones; EPS loops can TLE—use fixed iterations.
hints.3: Also: "minimize the maximum" / "maximize the minimum" ⇒ isValid + binary search on answer.

tradeoffs.topic: Linear scan of the answer space vs binary search on a monotonic space
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When feasibility is monotonic, binary search finds the min/max valid boundary in O(log(search space)) instead of trying answers linearly—especially when the range is huge (e.g. up to 10^{14}) and each check is O(N).

tradeoffs.topic: Floating-point while(r - l > EPS) vs fixed 100 iterations
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) over while(r - l > EPS) to avoid precision TLE on continuous / parametric float searches.

tradeoffs.topic: Array lower/upper bound vs binary search on answer
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sorted-array first/last position uses lower/upper bound; "minimize the maximum" / capacity / rate problems use an isValid(mid) parametric search over the answer.

gotchas.trap: Off-by-one when writing lower_bound / upper_bound (or bisect) by hand.
gotchas.correction: Practice the inclusive/exclusive update rules until first ≥ and first > land correctly without fencing errors.

gotchas.trap: Using while(r - l > EPS) for floating-point binary search.
gotchas.correction: Use a fixed loop for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) to avoid precision TLE.

gotchas.trap: Missing that "minimize the maximum" or "maximize the minimum" means binary search on answer.
gotchas.correction: Treat that wording as a hard giveaway: formulate isValid(mid) and binary-search the boundary (Book Allocation / Painter's Partition / capacity patterns).

gotchas.trap: Trying to invent a direct formula when the answer range is massive but a candidate is cheap to check.
gotchas.correction: If validating a guess is O(N) and the range is huge (e.g. up to 10^{14}), binary-search the answer with a monotone predicate.
